meta.title: Task completion notifications
meta.description: Sends system notifications at two moments: when your input is required (a tool asks for approval, a question awaits an answer, a plan needs review), and when a task stops. Stop notifications follow the turn's actual end reason — completed, failed, cancelled, output limit reached, blocked, or an unclean previous run — instead of always reading as completed. Notifications are posted by the DeepSeek Harness application itself, titled with the session name, and written in the interface language (Chinese or English); clicking one focuses the app and opens that task. Each pending request notifies once; the session you are viewing never notifies, while a finish in another session still does even when the app has focus, subagent sessions stay silent, and a pending request you saw but left unanswered is re-announced once after you switch away. Three switches under Settings › General control finish notifications, confirmation notifications, and a Dock unread count that clears as you open sessions; changes apply immediately. If notifications are disabled for the app in System Settings nothing appears and the session is unaffected.
